oil.summary: Crude sold off hard on the week — WTI down 6.4% and Brent off 6.1% — with today's session extending losses as the dominant macro story remains Washington's temporary easing of Russia oil sanctions. The Trump administration's move to relax sanctions and secure a diesel deal with Moscow drew bipartisan congressional criticism and sharp pushback from European allies, capping the geopolitical risk premium that had built up around Middle East disruptions. Headlines confirm the Iran conflict caused the largest oil and gas disruption on record, with tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf neighbor exports shuttered, yet Iranian oil itself continued flowing. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drone strikes reportedly halved Russian refining capacity in November, prompting Trump to publicly warn Kyiv to stand down. On the supply side, India posted record crude imports with Saudi shipments surging, Brazil is set to lead global production additions this year, and traders are actively seeking long-term Qatari crude deals for 2027. CME options-implied OPEC watch assigns a 77% probability of a production decrease at the May 2027 meeting.
drivers: US temporary easing of Russia oil sanctions and Trump-backed diesel deal with Moscow weighing heavily on the risk premium and driving week-long selloff
Strait of Hormuz disruptions — tanker strikes, Iranian threats, third US carrier deployment — remain a live tail risk but have so far failed to sustain a bullish bid
Rising non-OPEC supply (Brazil production boom, record Indian imports absorbing Saudi barrels) adding to bearish structural backdrop

gas.summary: The natural gas complex is sending mixed regional signals today. Henry Hub fell 3.74% on the session to $3.246/MMBtu, trimming part of its impressive +16.3% one-month rally, suggesting near-term profit-taking or milder weather expectations. European TTF moved in the opposite direction, surging 4.46% to €84.45/MWh, though it remains down 8.5% on the week — likely reflecting renewed supply-side anxiety given that the Iran conflict has been characterized as causing the largest oil and gas disruption on record, with the Iraq gas field drone alarm adding to Hormuz-corridor jitters. News flow for this sector is relatively thin today beyond the geopolitical overhang: Australia's federal government is exploring a gas phase-out clause in its domestic reservation scheme, and Venezuela announced an AI-driven methane reduction initiative.
drivers: Henry Hub giving back gains on the session despite its strong monthly uptrend, diverging sharply from a rebounding TTF
Iran war-driven Middle East supply disruption — flagged as the largest oil and gas disruption on record — underpinning European gas nervousness and the TTF bounce
Australian gas reservation scheme negotiations, including a potential phase-out clause with the Greens, adding long-run demand uncertainty for LNG exporters

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs recovered 2.81% today to $78.40/EUA, though the contract remains down nearly 9% on the week and roughly 4% on the month, tracking the broader energy complex's slide. The TTF gas bounce of 4.46% is directionally supportive of EUAs given gas-fired generation marginal cost dynamics in Europe. News flow in this sector today is macro-thematic rather than price-specific. Hard data on US data-center electricity consumption is reportedly staggering, with AI demand continuing to drive structural upward pressure on US power demand — a trend analysts say has not been deterred by AI sector volatility. Egypt announced a solar push targeting 7,000 factories, aiming for 42% renewable electricity by 2030. Venezuela's AI-driven methane reduction program speaks to emissions efficiency rather than power markets directly.
drivers: EUA carbon prices bouncing modestly alongside a TTF gas rally, but remaining under pressure on the week as the broader energy selloff weighs on carbon sentiment
Staggering US data-center power consumption figures reinforcing the structural AI-driven electricity demand thesis, with no sign of slowdown
Egypt's large-scale solar industrialization program highlighting accelerating emerging-market renewable buildout, though with limited immediate EUA market impact
